My LoRA fine-tune runs out of GPU memory on a 24GB card. What should I try?

Try these in order: 1) lower per_device_train_batch_size to 1 and raise gradient_accumulation_steps to keep the effective batch size; 2) enable gradient checkpointing; 3) reduce max_length if most examples are shorter; 4) switch to QLoRA (4-bit base weights); 5) lower the LoRA rank or target fewer modules. Check memory after each change so you know which one helped.

My training loss goes to almost zero but the model is worse on the eval set.

That is overfitting: the model is memorizing the training examples. Reduce the number of epochs (often 1-3 is enough for SFT), add more diverse data, lower the learning rate, and keep watching validation loss so you can stop when it starts rising. Also check that your eval set is not too different from your training data.

How do I stop my eval set from leaking into training?

Split before any training or prompt tuning, split by group (customer, document or conversation) instead of by row, and deduplicate near-identical examples across the split. Then run an automated overlap check between train and eval prompts before every training run.

How do I protect an agent from prompt injection?

Treat everything the agent reads from files, web pages or tool outputs as data, not instructions. Give tools the least privilege needed, require human approval for actions that write, send or delete, run code in a sandbox, and never let tool output change the agent's permissions.
